exposure: Body Mass Index (BMI) categories (Normal, Overweight, Obesity)
cohort: The study included 191 women undergoing IVF/ICSI cycles with non-donor oocytes, categorized by BMI as normal, overweight, or obese.
finding: An increased Body Mass Index (BMI) significantly reduces pregnancy, implantation, and live birth rates while affecting embryo development in women undergoing IVF procedures.
